#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --job-name="1RST_fe_complex"
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=24
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=2G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --array=0-19

module purge
module load cuda/11.4 gromacs/2021.4

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE

export COMPLEX=1RST_pep
export TASK_ID=$(printf "%02d" $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID)

mkdir lambda.${TASK_ID}
cd lambda.${TASK_ID}

mkdir ENMIN
cd ENMIN
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/ENMIN/enmin.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../../$COMPLEX.gro -p ../../$COMPLEX.top -o enmin.tpr
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s enmin.tpr -deffnm enmin -ntmpi 1

cd ../
mkdir NVT
cd NVT
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/NVT/nvt.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../ENMIN/enmin.gro -p ../../$COMPLEX.top -o nvt.tpr -r ../ENMIN/enmin.gro
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s nvt.tpr -deffnm nvt -ntmpi 1

cd ../
mkdir NPT
cd NPT
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/NPT/npt.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../NVT/nvt.gro -t ../NVT/nvt.cpt -p ../../$COMPLEX.top  -o npt.tpr -r ../NVT/nvt.gro
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s npt.tpr -deffnm npt -ntmpi 1

cd ../
mkdir PROD
cd PROD
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/PROD/prod.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../NPT/npt.gro -t ../NPT/npt.cpt -p ../../$COMPLEX.top  -o prod.tpr -r ../NPT/npt.gro
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s prod.tpr -deffnm prod -dhdl dhdl -ntmpi 1

cd ../../

reasons: Resource Mismatch: The script requests 24 tasks (`--ntasks=24`) for each job in the array, but the `gmx mdrun` commands are explicitly configured to use only a single MPI task (`-ntmpi 1`). This will result in 23 allocated CPU cores sitting idle for each of the 20 array jobs, leading to significant resource waste.
issues: The environment variable `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is set using `$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE`, which may not be defined by Slurm in all configurations. It is more robust to request cores explicitly with `--cpus-per-task` and then use the `$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK` variable.

The `gmx mdrun` commands do not use the `-ntomp` flag to specify the number of OpenMP threads. While GROMACS will fall back to using the `OMP_NUM_THREADS` environment variable, explicitly setting `-ntomp` in the command makes the script's intent clearer and less prone to environment-related errors.

For a typical single-node, single-GPU GROMACS simulation, a more efficient resource request would be `--ntasks=1` and `--cpus-per-task=<num_cores_for_threading>`, which would correctly allocate resources for a hybrid MPI/OpenMP execution model that uses one MPI task and multiple OpenMP threads.
